subject.title: [Bug]: In msteams channel messages, OpenClaw can't access inbound attachments

question: Should Microsoft Teams non-personal Graph media fallback be automatic, default-off behind channels.msteams.graphMediaFallback, or reconciled into one combined attachment repair?
rationale: Current main avoids noisy Graph lookups by requiring extracted attachment IDs, but live Teams evidence shows real uploaded files can arrive without those IDs; the default affects existing deployments through Graph call volume, permissions expectations, diagnostics, and message-delivery behavior.

options.title: Accept narrow group-chat opt-in
options.body: Land a default-off graphMediaFallback for group chats after its runtime scope and tests match the documented group-chat-only contract, while the broader channel URL repair lands separately.

options.title: Land the broader channel repair without new config
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90738 or an equivalent no-new-config branch as the canonical fix, accepting best-effort Graph lookup for non-personal Teams HTML stubs.

options.title: Require one reconciled PR
options.body: Ask for one msteams media PR that covers group chats, channel team GUIDs, thread-reply URLs, docs, and upgrade behavior before closing this issue.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow group-chat opt-in
recommendation.body: Land a default-off graphMediaFallback for group chats after its runtime scope and tests match the documented group-chat-only contract, while the broader channel URL repair lands separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is a Teams plugin compatibility/product-default choice, and steipete has the strongest available maintainer-routing signal from current-main history and the issue timeline.
